title: Aeronautical Charts and Publications
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 9 covering chart types, symbols, and publications

cards.back:
SECTIONAL: 1:500,000 (1" ≈ 6.86 NM)
• Most common VFR chart
• Updated every 56 days

TAC (Terminal Area): 1:250,000 (1" ≈ 3.43 NM)
• Greater detail for busy terminal areas

WORLD AERONAUTICAL (WAC): 1:1,000,000
• For long-distance navigation
• Less detail

CLASS B: Solid BLUE lines
CLASS C: Solid MAGENTA lines
CLASS D: Dashed BLUE lines
CLASS E (surface): Dashed MAGENTA lines
CLASS E (above 700/1200'): Faded magenta tint

Brackets [ceiling/floor]: Altitudes in hundreds of feet MSL

BLUE: Towered airport (control tower operating)
MAGENTA: Non-towered airport

Symbol shapes indicate services:
• Circle with runways = hard surface
• Open circle = soft surface only
• 'R' in circle = private
• Seaplane symbol = seaplane base

Format: Name (Identifier)
Below: Elevation, Lighting, Runway length

Example: CENTERVILLE (CTL)
 1250 L 72

• 1250 = Field elevation (ft MSL)
• L = Lighting available
• 72 = Longest runway (7,200 ft)
• Star = ATIS available

• Largest bold number in each quadrangle
• Format: First digit(s) = thousands, last digit = hundreds
• Example: '45' = 4,500 feet MSL

Includes:
• Highest terrain
• Highest obstruction
• Safety buffer added

Useful for VFR minimum altitude planning

Small dot with tower:
• Less than 1,000' AGL

Large dot with tower (group):
• 1,000' AGL or higher

Star/Lightning bolt = High-intensity lighting

Numbers show:
• Top = MSL altitude
• (Bottom) = AGL height

P = Prohibited (never enter)
R = Restricted (may be active, permission needed)
W = Warning (hazardous over international waters)
MOA = Military Operations Area (VFR may enter)
A = Alert Area (high pilot training activity)
CFA = Controlled Firing Area (ceases when traffic detected)

IR = IFR Military Training Routes
VR = VFR Military Training Routes

Routes with 4 digits: Operations at/below 1,500' AGL
Routes with 3 digits: At least one segment above 1,500' AGL

Gray lines on charts with route number
High-speed military training

VOR: Compass rose with center dot
VORTAC: VOR with 3-sided box
VOR/DME: VOR with small square
NDB: Solid dot with circle
DME only: 'DME' label

Box around identifier = NAVAID part of Federal Airway system

Contains for each airport:
• Location and communications
• Runway information (length, width, surface)
• Lighting, approaches available
• Services (fuel, repairs)
• Special procedures
• NOTAMs
• Frequencies

Updated every 56 days

Depicted as:
• Magenta flag symbol
• Name in magenta

Used for:
• Position reports
• Traffic advisories
• Local area familiarity
• Arrival/departure procedures

Common near busy airports

VFR Flyway: Suggested route for VFR traffic
• Printed on TAC chart
• Helps avoid busy terminal areas

VFR Transition Route: Specific route through Class B
• Requires clearance
• Specific altitudes
• Printed on TAC chart

• 30 NM radius from primary Class B airport
• Depicted by solid blue circle
• Transponder with Mode C required
• ADS-B Out also required
• Exception: Aircraft without engine-driven electrical system

Depicted as:
• Parachute symbol
• MSL altitude
• Frequency (if available)

Caution:
• Active without notice
• Traffic may be circling
• Jumpers difficult to see

• Dashed magenta lines
• Connect points of equal magnetic variation
• Show degrees East or West
• 'Agonic line' = zero variation

Used to convert:
• True heading to magnetic
• 'East is least, West is best'

Lines of LATITUDE:
• Horizontal, parallel to equator
• Degrees N or S

Lines of LONGITUDE:
• Vertical, converge at poles
• Degrees E or W from Prime Meridian

1° latitude = 60 NM
1 minute latitude = 1 NM

LOW ALTITUDE (L-charts):
• Below 18,000' MSL
• Victor Airways (V-xxx)

HIGH ALTITUDE (H-charts):
• 18,000' MSL and above
• Jet Routes (J-xxx)

Updated every 56 days
Show MEAs, MOCAs, airways, NAVAIDs

Contains:
• Instrument Approach Procedures (IAPs)
• Standard Instrument Departures (SIDs)
• Standard Terminal Arrivals (STARs)
• Airport diagrams
• Takeoff/alternate minimums

Updated every 28 days

Always use CURRENT charts!

Update cycles:
• Sectional/TAC: 56 days
• IFR En Route: 56 days
• Terminal Procedures: 28 days
• Chart Supplement: 56 days

Expired charts may have incorrect:
• Frequencies
• Procedures
• Airspace

GREEN: Lower elevations
YELLOW/TAN: Higher elevations
BROWN: Mountains

Contour lines:
• Connect points of equal elevation
• Closer lines = steeper terrain

Shaded relief shows terrain features

Depicted as:
• Solid black line
• TRSA label

Characteristics:
• Participation voluntary
• Service similar to Class C
• No transponder requirement
• Good place for student practice

Depicted as:
• Dotted line pattern
• May have altitude restriction noted

Recommendations:
• Maintain 2,000' AGL
• Avoid disturbing wildlife
• Check for specific restrictions

National Parks/Wilderness Areas:
• Boundaries shown
• May have altitude restrictions

Recommendations:
• 2,000' AGL minimum encouraged
• No commercial air tours without permit
• Noise-sensitive areas

NOT directly depicted!

Class G exists where no other airspace is designated:
• Below Class E (where E starts at 700' or 1,200')
• Generally uncontrolled
• No communication required

Infer from absence of other airspace symbology

Official FAA sources:
• faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav

Free digital products:
• VFR charts (raster and geo-referenced)
• IFR charts
• Chart Supplement

Third-party EFB apps also available
Always verify currency
